skills.name: Other propositions and translation into standard form

note.text: Translate only by checking the direction of restriction; translate not all as some…not. Treat singular claims under an explicit convention and clarify indefinite scope. Preserve exceptions and both parts of compound claims rather than forcing every sentence into one blanket categorical statement.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to translate only and not all accurately, recognise singular and indefinite cases, and preserve an exception. Builds on: sentence parts, categorical forms, conditionals and disjunctions. Leads to: Term Two’s translation into symbolic logic and later argument analysis.

sections.heading: Preserve scope, not word order
sections.text: Only club members are voters means All voters are club members: being a member is required for voting in the fictional rule. It does not say every member votes. Not all members are voters means Some members are not voters. Identify who is restricted, then choose subject, predicate, quantifier and quality. An accurate rewrite preserves meaning even when it changes word order.

sections.heading: Singular and indefinite claims
sections.text: Bih is a member is singular: it concerns an individual. One explicit standardisation treats S as persons identical with Bih, giving All persons identical with Bih are members; assume the name denotes a person. Teachers should confirm their course’s singular convention. Members are readers, without an explicit quantifier, is indefinite in the traditional classroom sense. Ask whether context means all or some; do not guess from the plural alone.

sections.heading: Do not erase an exception
sections.text: For this explicit rule, every library book except damaged library books is loanable, and none of the damaged books is loanable. Preserve both parts: All undamaged library books are loanable items; No damaged library books are loanable items. One blanket All library books are loanable items would erase the exception. Other compound claims may require more than one categorical statement, or the conditional/disjunctive forms just studied.

key_words.meaning: only restricts one class to another; distinct from exclusive OR
lacking an explicit quantifier in this school terminology
expressing an exception that must be preserved

mistake.wrong: Only members are voters means every member votes.
mistake.right: It means every voter is a member.
mistake.why: Only makes membership necessary for being a voter, without asserting that all members vote.

worked_example.problem: Translate Only badge holders are club voters.
steps: The restricted group is club voters.
Every club voter must be within the badge-holder class.
The claim leaves open whether all badge holders vote.
worked_example.answer: All club voters are badge holders.

cards.idea: Only S are P translates as All P are S.
example: Only members are voters: All voters are members.

cards.idea: A singular claim specifies an individual.
example: Bih is a member differs from an explicit all-members claim.

cards.idea: Not all means at least one exception, not no members.
example: Not all S are P: Some S are not P.

pick.r: Some club members are not badge holders.
w: No club members are badge holders.
All club members are badge holders.
Some club members are badge holders.
e: No excludes every shared member, stronger than not all.
That asserts what the original denies.
That affirms membership but does not supply the required exception.
pick.y: Denying universal inclusion requires an existing S outside P: O.

pick.q: The isolated sentence “Club members are badge holders” gives no explicit quantifier. What should you do before fixing A or I?
pick.r: Ask whether the context intends every subject member or merely some.
w: Always force A because every plural noun means all.
Always force I because all indefinite sentences mean some but not all.
Treat it as E solely because the quantifier is missing.
e: Plural wording alone does not settle universal scope.
That invents both a fixed quantifier and a not-all restriction.
A missing quantifier does not establish universal denial.
pick.y: An indefinite statement needs contextual scope; do not manufacture certainty from missing information.

questions.prompt: Find the incorrect claim, then read the reason for the correction.

right.text: Only S are P restricts every P to S.
right.explain: This is a correct rule: Only S are P restricts every P to S. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

right.text: Not all S are P has O meaning.
right.explain: This is a correct rule: Not all S are P has O meaning. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

right.text: A singular proposition concerns a specified individual.
right.explain: This is a correct rule: A singular proposition concerns a specified individual. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

right.text: An unclear quantifier may need contextual clarification.
right.explain: This is a correct rule: An unclear quantifier may need contextual clarification. Look for a claim that breaks a rule taught in Learn.

wrong.text: Only S are P always translates as All S are P.
wrong.explain: Preserve the restriction: All P are S, not the reverse.

wrong.text: An indefinite plural sentence always explicitly asserts all.
wrong.explain: The intended scope needs context; a plural noun is not an explicit all.

wrong.text: All S except Q are P is fully preserved by simply writing All S are P.
wrong.explain: That discards the exception. The permitted S and the excluded Q need separate treatment.

wrong.text: A single A/E/I/O sentence always preserves every compound ordinary-language claim.
wrong.explain: Some claims need more than one categorical statement, or a compound symbolic form.

pick.q: A fictional rule says: All club members outside the excluded group are voters, and none of the excluded club members are voters. Which rewrite preserves both parts?
pick.r: All non-excluded club members are voters; no excluded club members are voters.
w: All club members are voters.
No club members are voters.
All voters are club members.
e: This erases the stated excluded group.
This erases the permitted non-excluded group.
This reverses class inclusion and says nothing about the exception.
pick.y: Keep both the affirmative rule for the non-excluded class and the negative rule for the excluded class.
